conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hello, I'm Dr. Lee. I’ll be taking care of you during your stay. Can you tell me what’s been going on with the nausea and vomiting?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Hi, Doctor. It’s been two weeks of constant nausea, and for the last two days, I’ve been vomiting. I can barely keep anything down—just small amounts of yogurt or pudding.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. Any fever, chills, or abdominal pain? Or changes in your bowel movements?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No fever or chills. My stomach doesn’t hurt, and I haven’t had diarrhea. I did notice my stool was brown, no blood.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay. Your labs from the ER look stable—no signs of infection or pancreatitis. We’ll start you on fluids and a medication called Compazine for nausea.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That sounds good. I’ve had this for months, and GI hasn’t found a cause yet.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, I see you had an EUS recently that showed a dilated bile duct, but no stones or strictures. We’ll keep monitoring and see if reducing your OxyContin helps—sometimes narcotics can worsen nausea.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I didn’t know that. I’ve been on 20 mg twice a day. Is it safe to lower it?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll reduce it to 10 mg twice a day for now. We’re also starting you on Cymbalta for nerve pain and mood, which may help overall.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I trust your judgment.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your platelet count is low at 92, down to 73 this morning. We’re watching it closely. It might be from the antibiotics you were on for cellulitis.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is that dangerous? I’ve had low platelets before.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s concerning, but not critical. We’ll keep an eye on it. Since your cellulitis is much better, we’ll continue Keflex as planned.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: My leg looks better, yes. The redness is fading.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good. Your heart function is stable—EF around 55-60%. We held your torsemide because you weren’t eating, but we’ll restart it today as you start tolerating more fluids.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve been feeling a bit swollen in my legs. Is that from the heart?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, mild congestion is chronic for you. The chest X-ray shows that. But you’re not overloaded, so we’ll go slow with the diuretic.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We did a CT scan of your head to rule out any brain issues causing nausea. It’s normal—no bleeding or stroke.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s a relief. I was worried about that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Me too. Everything points to chronic nausea, possibly from meds or gut motility. The Compazine seems to be helping—you haven’t vomited since yesterday?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No, not since morning. I even sipped some broth.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Great. We’ll advance you to a clear liquid diet and see how you do.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Morning. Your platelets are up to 87 today—trending in the right direction. Hemoglobin is stable at 9.6.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s good. Should I still be worried about bleeding?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not at this point. We’ll keep monitoring. Your INR is 2.4—perfect for warfarin. You were a bit high before admission, so we adjusted the dose.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I remember they held a dose when it was high. I’m glad it’s stable now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes. And your heart rhythm is still atrial fibrillation, but rate-controlled with metoprolol.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Doctor, I noticed some blood in my stool this morning. Just streaks, not a lot.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Thanks for letting me know. The nurse checked—it’s guaiac positive. You have a history of hemorrhoids, so it’s likely from that. But we’ll need GI to follow up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Should I be worried? I’m on warfarin.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s not a lot of blood, and your hemoglobin hasn’t dropped. But yes, we’ll make sure GI evaluates it soon.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing well. You’ve been on a regular diet since lunch and no nausea. We’re planning to discharge you tomorrow.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s great! What about my meds?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll stay on Keflex for cellulitis prevention. OxyContin is now 10 mg twice a day. We’re adding prochlorperazine for nausea as needed, and Cymbalta daily.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my warfarin and torsemide?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, both back to your usual doses. We’ll send a note to your PCP to check a CBC and QTc interval soon.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your labs this morning are stable. Platelets are 91, hemoglobin 9.6. You’re cleared for discharge.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. What should I watch for at home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Weigh yourself daily. Call if you gain more than 3 pounds. Watch for worsening nausea, or if you see more blood in your stool. Follow up with your PCP in a week and GI soon after.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thank you for all your help.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Take care, and we’ll see you in clinic if needed.
